title: Starter Pack Syntax
pitch: The visitor is dealt a subject card for a thing rather than a person (a rainy Monday, a rink snack bar at the second intermission, a first week with a new roguelike) and fills a cobblestone-style mosaic of six tiles from a tray of hand-drawn vector items. A live grammar linter labels every tile with its job (the unmistakable anchor, the niche specific, the filler, the ironic turn) and scores the pack on balance, recognisability and sting. A reverse mode shows a finished pack and asks which subject it was; any pack exports as a PNG and as a shareable link.
whyNow: The starter pack format dates to 2014 per Wikipedia and Know Your Meme, and its structure (a plain title plus a few images that stand for a situation) is timeless, so the hook is the grammar, not a news item. The page also takes a seasonal subject deck keyed to the run date. No claim is made about which meme format dominates this week.

research.summary: The starter pack is a well-documented collage format: a plain title plus a handful of images that together stand for a stereotype or situation. Wikipedia and Know Your Meme both date it to a Twitter post of 27 September 2014, and the Daily Dot also places its growth in late September to November 2014. Researchers are starting to describe memes as having rules of composition (a 2025 Cambridge University Press book on a grammar of memes, and a student corpus project on meme syntax), which supports a page that makes slots and roles explicit. Every subject in the page is a thing or situation, never a group of people or a private person, and all art is drawn in code. Spinoff history (Loyal But Dangerous) and this week's trending formats each rest on one source and are not stated as fact.

facts.claim: Wikipedia and Know Your Meme both trace the starter pack meme to a Twitter post dated 27 September 2014.
Per Know Your Meme, dedicated starter pack curation accounts followed in mid-November 2014; the Daily Dot likewise reports a surge of Twitter mentions in November 2014.
A 2025 Cambridge University Press book by Barbara Dancygier and Lieven Vandelanotte argues that memes are multimodal and follow rules of composition and interpretation (a grammar of memes).
A student corpus project, Such Syntax, Much Meme, analyses the syntactic structure of text-based memes, so naming the slots and roles of a meme format has academic precedent.

As of 2026-10-10, per Know Your Meme (entry marked as under research, single source), the Loyal But Dangerous starter pack spinoff began on the starter pack subreddit in May 2021 and later versions often replace one image.
As of 2026-10-10, no single meme format could be confirmed as dominant this month: only one commercial roundup is dated October 2026 and other lists are older (single source, not presented as fact).

design.coreLoop: Draw a subject card, fill six tiles from a twelve-item tray, read the linter's verdict on each tile's role, swap items to fix balance and sting, then lock the pack. Repetition stays interesting because each subject has its own hand-authored item matrix (typicality plus role tags), the linter explains why a swap helps, and reverse mode flips the skill from composing to decoding.
sophisticationHooks: Grammar linter: every item carries per-subject typicality 0 to 3 and a role tag (anchor, specific, filler, turn); rules flag two competing anchors, no turn, or all filler, and name the fix
Reverse mode: a finished pack is shown and the visitor picks the subject from four; distractor subjects are chosen to overlap on filler items so the specifics decide
Cobblestone mosaic layout: one large anchor tile and five irregular tiles packed with a mortar gap, rendered in SVG and exported to PNG through canvas
Daily subject seeded from the run date, 12 subjects, shareable URL hash holding subject plus six item ids, so a friend can open your exact pack
design.scopeForOneDay: Shrunk from the scout's size. Built: 12 subject cards (things and situations only), about 48 drawn SVG items made from simple geometric glyphs and shared parts, per-subject matrix with tag-derived defaults and hand-tuned top three items, linter rules and scoring with stated reasons, build mode, reverse mode, PNG export via canvas, URL hash state, light and dark, reduced motion, keyboard placement (arrow plus enter), and an about panel that lists only verified sources. Cut: free-text item entry, uploaded images, any real photo, multiplayer, seasonal deck beyond a handful of date-keyed subjects.
risks: Hand-authoring subject-by-item typicality values is the main time sink; mitigate with tag-derived defaults and hand-tuning only the top three items per subject, and cut to 12 subjects if behind

Stereotype drift: subjects are restricted to things and situations, never groups or named people, and the about panel states the rule; item names must not use real brands or logos, all art is drawn in code

The origin facts rest on Wikipedia, Know Your Meme and the Daily Dot, none of which were opened today; the page presents them as 'per Wikipedia and Know Your Meme' with the date checked, and makes no claim about this week's trends
Unverified claims stay off the page as fact: the Loyal But Dangerous spinoff history and any trending-format claim are shown as 'as of 2026-10-10, per Know Your Meme' or omitted
Scoring can feel arbitrary; the linter must show its reasons, and the score is labelled as a game score, not a verdict on humour
Shared link carries only subject and item ids in the URL hash; no network request, no personal data

verification.notes: The 2014 origin is confirmed by several independent search results and the grammar-of-memes book exists, but no page could be opened (knowyourmeme.com failed, other hosts already failed today). The scout's Object Labeling claim was unconfirmed and dropped, the Reddit-born framing was corrected to a Twitter origin, and scope was cut to 12 subjects and about 48 items.
